evidence.reason: Public proposal entrypoint wrapping ApplyLog; creates LogCommand logFuture delivered over applyCh (api.go:849).
Public replicated membership-change entrypoint; all four ID-based membership APIs funnel into requestConfigChange (raft.go:115).
Peer-to-peer RPC ingress (rpcCh consumer) is a separate internal surface and is excluded as workload input.

external_input.boundary: Public Raft API of the pinned github.com/hashicorp/raft module (Raft methods, Transport abstraction, InmemTransport, observer/future mechanisms, module-provided in-memory stores). Real TCP transports, external durable stores, application FSM semantics, and fuzzy/raft-compat/bench trees are outside.
external_input.reason: Proposal and membership-change workload entrypoints are public, documented APIs that return completion futures (ApplyFuture with Index/Response; IndexFuture for membership changes). The internal applyCh/configurationChangeCh delivery and ErrNotLeader rejection semantics are observable through the returned futures. Barrier and VerifyLeader are barriers, and Bootstrap/Snapshot/Restore are maintenance operations excluded by the testing contract.
limitations: Apply returns ErrLeadershipLost if leadership is lost mid-apply; whether the write survived is unknowable by design (api.go:810-814).
Future.Error() must be called before Future.Index()/Response()/Configuration() (future.go:13-65).
GetConfiguration, Barrier, and VerifyLeader can block forever if enqueued concurrently with shutdown (raft_test.go:40-42 documents this known quirk).
usage_examples:
c := raft.MakeCluster(3, t, nil)
leader := c.Leader() // *raft.Raft
future := leader.Apply([]byte("set x=1"), 0)
if err := future.Error(); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
idx, resp := future.Index(), future.Response()
external_input.test_support_reason: The existing public API directly provides all workload entrypoints and blocking completion futures; a test cluster (MakeCluster/MakeClusterCustom, testing.go:733-858) plus leader.Apply/AddVoter suffices with no additional target code.

membership: AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter -> requestConfigChange -> configurationChangeCh -> LogConfiguration entry -> commit -> ConfigurationStore.StoreConfiguration
rejected-on-follower: applyCh/configurationChangeCh are answered ErrNotLeader in runFollower/runCandidate (raft.go:173-196, 386-394)

protocol_ingress_excluded.reason: Peer protocol ingress enters through trans.Consumer()/rpcCh and is handled by processRPC (raft.go:1390, 1396-1412), a distinct internal surface from the public workload APIs; it is excluded from workload entrypoints.

evidence.reason: Internal timer helper used exclusively by protocol loops, not a public workload entrypoint.

timer_and_internal_events_excluded.reason: Election/heartbeat/commit/snapshot timers (randomTimeout call sites raft.go:163,310; replication.go:169,402,495; snapshot.go:75) and internal channels (fsmMutateCh, fsmSnapshotCh, leaderNotifyCh) are internal events; only the public Apply/membership methods are declared as workload entrypoints.

evidence.reason: Creates LogCommand logFuture, enqueues on applyCh; future completes when the log is committed and applied.
Submits configurationChangeRequest through requestConfigChange (raft.go:115), the membership workload path.

workload_entrypoint.reason: Application work originating outside the protocol is submitted through Apply/ApplyLog (proposals) and AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter (replicated membership changes); both return futures blocking on commit, documented at api.go:804-852 and api.go:938-1007. Barrier/VerifyLeader/Bootstrap/Snapshot/Restore are excluded as barrier/maintenance/administrative operations.

evidence.reason: Target-defined stop: closes shutdownCh, sets Shutdown state, returns a future that blocks until background goroutines exit and closes a WithClose transport.
Reconstruction boundary: a fresh *Raft over the same stores/FSM/transport resumes as the same logical node, replaying snapshot and log state.

lifecycle_control.boundary: Public Raft API and in-process stores (InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore/FileSnapshotStore) inside the boundary; process supervision and external durable store implementations outside.
lifecycle_control.reason: Stop (Raft.Shutdown with goroutine join) and restore (reconstruction via NewRaft over the same caller-owned stores) compose directly into a complete availability cycle with explicit, target-defined semantics: the stopped instance is terminal and a new instance resumes the same logical node. InmemTransport Disconnect/Connect is partition isolation, not lifecycle unavailability, and is called out as such.
limitations: No pause/resume exists; Shutdown is terminal for the instance and closes a WithClose transport (future.go:176-178), so the test must supply a fresh or reconnected transport on reconstruction.
Persistence of term/vote/log across the cycle depends on the caller's store implementations (InmemStore is volatile in-process).
Network isolation alone (Disconnect) does not stop local protocol activity and is therefore not lifecycle unavailability.
entrypoints: cluster.Close / shutdown helpers in package testing support
lifecycle_control.test_support_reason: Shutdown() and NewRaft() are directly usable public operations; no new target code is needed to make a node unavailable and bring it back as the same logical node.
execution_paths: stop: Shutdown() closes shutdownCh (set in api.go:1017), sets state Shutdown (api.go:1019); run/runFSM/runSnapshots goroutines exit on <-shutdownCh (raft.go:139,252,436,683); shutdownFuture.Error waits via waitShutdown and closes the transport when it implements WithClose (future.go:167-180)

restore: new *Raft built over the same caller-owned LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore/FSM with the same LocalID resumes protocol activity; NewRaft replays snapshot + log configuration entries (api.go:592-625); restart pattern used by the package's own tests (raft_test.go:1004, 2788)
network partition (not lifecycle): InmemTransport Connect/Disconnect/DisconnectAll (inmem_transport.go:214-251) isolate peers while the node keeps running local protocol loops

evidence.reason: close(r.shutdownCh); r.setState(Shutdown) under shutdownLock; idempotent second call returns a nil-raft future.

stop_boundary.reason: Shutdown() makes the node unavailable: shutdownCh close is observed by run (raft.go:139), runFollower (raft.go:252), runCandidate (raft.go:436), runLeader (raft.go:683), and runFSM; state becomes Shutdown and subsequent API calls return ErrRaftShutdown.

evidence.reason: NewRaft restores latest snapshot and replays configuration entries, so reconstruction resumes prior protocol state.

restart_or_recovery_boundary.reason: The same logical node becomes available again by constructing a new Raft over the same LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore/FSM (NewRaft, api.go:500); state is restored from the caller-owned stores (restoreSnapshot at api.go:593 and configuration scan at api.go:597-608), and the same pattern is exercised in-package (raft_test.go:1004, 2788, 3105).

evidence.reason: Signature declares caller-provided stores/FSM/transport; Raft never creates them.

state_ownership_defined.reason: NewRaft takes fsm FSM, logs LogStore, stable StableStore, snaps SnapshotStore, trans Transport (api.go:500); the Raft struct stores them as plain fields (api.go:101-185). State ownership is explicitly the caller's stores and FSM, not the Raft instance.

evidence.reason: Volatile in-memory LogStore/StableStore; durability is determined by the store implementation the caller supplies.

persistent_volatile_semantics_defined.reason: InmemStore is explicitly an in-memory store (inmem_store.go:25); FileSnapshotStore persists snapshots to a directory; durable log/stable implementations are caller-provided and out of boundary. Shutdown is documented as 'not a graceful operation' (api.go:1009-1011), and the report does not invent crash/persistence semantics beyond what the chosen stores define.

evidence.reason: The only in-boundary transport exposes a fixed buffered consumerCh (make(chan RPC, 16)) that Raft itself drains; there is no test-visible capture cache, take/drop/clear, or continuation control.

Observations (RequestVoteRequest, LeaderObservation, PeerObservation, FailedHeartbeat) are emitted during/after processing into caller channels with no delivery control, so they are a post-entry notification primitive, not a controlled cache.

Public interface seam where all protocol output (inbound Consumer() channel and outbound send/pipeline methods) crosses the boundary; a capture transport would have to be added by the harness or the package since none ships.

message_capture.boundary: Transport abstraction, InmemTransport, RPC struct, and observer mechanism inside the boundary; real network transports outside.
message_capture.gap: No target-provided message cache: cannot enumerate, take, drop, or clear protocol messages before delivery on any path; the only current interception options are test-side reimplementation of the transport (caller-created collection, a primitive) or racing the protocol consumer.
message_capture.reason: No in-scope path has a controlled, test-visible capture cache today: the InmemTransport consumer channel is exclusively consumed by Raft and inaccessible after NewRaft; observers are post-delivery notifications; there is no enumerate/Take/Drop/Clear API anywhere. However, all protocol output crosses the public Transport seam, so a low-intrusion change (an in-package capture transport that owns the consumer channel and queues outbound calls, or optional capture hooks on InmemTransport) can complete every path. Heartbeat fast-path handling exists only via SetHeartbeatHandler and is a no-op for InmemTransport.
limitations: InmemTransport.AppendEntries/RequestVote block the sender until a response or 500ms timeout (inmem_transport.go:166-200); a capture point that holds inbound RPCs must eventually respond through RPC.Respond or the sender observes a timeout.
RPC does not carry the sender address; routing info for inbound messages must be read from the request's RPCHeader (ID/Addr, raft.go:35-41).
If a transport uses SetHeartbeatHandler for a heartbeat fast-path, capture must also hook that handler; InmemTransport ignores it.
Responses are not separate cacheable messages: they complete the original RPC via RespChan or the pipeline future and cannot be captured as independent instances.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Add the capture transport under a new file in the raft package (or extend InmemTransport), keeping production defaults unchanged.
message_capture.test_support_reason: Existing primitives (Transport interface, RPC/RespChan, InmemTransport consumer channel, observers) allow a test to see messages only by replacing the transport (a caller-created collection, i.e. a primitive) or by reading post-processing notifications; no complete capture cache with continuation ownership and Take/Drop/Clear exists in the target.
suggested_changes: Add a small in-package capture transport (e.g., raft.testCaptureTransport wrapping any Transport) that owns the Consumer() channel so the capture point is the protocol consumer, and queues outbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot/TimeoutNow/pipeline calls with target routing; expose Enumerate/Take/Drop/Clear on the queue.
Alternatively add an opt-in capture mode to InmemTransport (a replaceable consumer channel plus outbound queues) while keeping the default path unchanged.
Expose an in-package wrapper for AppendPipeline that records AppendFuture completion so the outbound-pipeline path is captured with the same cache semantics.
execution_paths: inbound-consumer: requests arrive at a node via Transport.Consumer(); Raft stores the channel as rpcCh (api.go:561) and the main loop is the sole consumer (raft.go:169,323,683), dispatching in processRPC (raft.go:1390); responses complete the original exchange through RPC.RespChan (transport.go:18-27). Heartbeats are AppendEntries with empty entries on the same channel for InmemTransport (SetHeartbeatHandler is a no-op, inmem_transport.go:72-75); a fast-path handler exists as a separate control surface for transports that support it.

outbound-send: synchronous Transport.AppendEntries (replication.go:231,412), RequestVote/RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot, TimeoutNow calls; each returns by copying into a caller-owned response value; a test-visible capture point would sit at these methods, holding the call until the test takes/drops/clears/injects.

outbound-pipeline: Transport.AppendEntriesPipeline (replication.go:452) returns an AppendPipeline whose AppendEntries returns an AppendFuture with its own Consumer() channel (transport.go:112-123; inmem_transport.go:259-309); completion is asynchronous via future.respond.

evidence.reason: Defines the completion mechanism of every captured inbound RPC; injection must preserve this RespChan so the original sender is not orphaned.
The normal request-handler boundary for inbound messages; injecting a cached request means delivering it here via the transport consumer channel, not fabricating a response.
Shows the outbound send path and its synchronous response copy; a capture/injection wrapper must replicate response copying and timeout behavior truthfully.

message_injection.boundary: Same message-control boundary and path partition as message_capture.
message_injection.gap: No cache from which to Take a selected message, and no public deliver/ingest API; injection today would require the test to reimplement transport routing (primitive) and cannot preserve cache effects because no cache exists.
message_injection.reason: Injection is feasible in both accepted forms once a capture cache exists: separated (cache Take returns the message plus routing info — target address for outbound, RPCHeader ID/Addr for inbound — and the test owns the real transports/instances to call the normal input operation) or combined single-call facade on a capture transport. Because the target ships no cache and no deliver-RPC API, injection is not directly usable today; the same low-intrusion capture transport completes it on all three shared paths, preserving message direction and the RespChan/future completion mechanisms.
limitations: Cache effects for synchronous failure (sender-side timeout) and unconfirmed async delivery (pipeline inflight) must be defined by the harness transport; the target defines none.
Injecting an inbound request whose sender already timed out leaves a dangling RespChan send unless the harness completes it (transport.go:25-27).

Fabricating or completing a response does not count as injecting a cached request; only a cached response instance may enter a response boundary, and in this codebase responses complete the original RPC rather than forming an independent inbound path.
message_injection.suggested_direction: Ship the injection operations together with the capture transport so capture and injection share one cache and path partition.
entrypoints: Transport consumer channel (injection target for inbound requests)
Transport send methods and AppendPipeline (injection targets for outbound requests)
message_injection.test_support_reason: The Transport seam plus RPC.RespChan are the underlying plumbing: they make injection possible in principle, but there is no target-side cache to Take from and no complete injection interface, so a harness/package addition is required.
suggested_changes: With the proposed capture transport, provide Take(target) that removes and returns the selected message plus routing (peer address; inbound RPCHeader), and a documented normal input call per path: enqueue onto the owned consumer channel for inbound, invoke the underlying transport method for outbound-send, invoke AppendPipeline for outbound-pipeline.
Optionally provide a combined single-call facade on the capture transport: Take + validate target + invoke normal input + update cache state in one method (without implying atomicity).
Define and document cache effects for success (entry removed), synchronous failure (entry removed with error surfaced), and unconfirmed async delivery (entry removed or retained by explicit policy).
execution_paths: inbound-consumer: normal input boundary is the channel returned by Transport.Consumer(), drained by the Raft main loop (raft.go:169,323,683) and dispatched by processRPC/processHeartbeat (raft.go:1390-1436); injection means delivering a captured request RPC (with its RespChan) onto that owned channel, preserving direction and the response completion mechanism

outbound-send: normal input boundary is the Transport send method for the message's own direction (AppendEntries at replication.go:231,412; RequestVote/RequestPreVote; InstallSnapshot; TimeoutNow); a captured outbound request is injected by invoking the real transport's method with the captured args, target, and response pointer
outbound-pipeline: normal input boundary is AppendPipeline.AppendEntries (transport.go:115); injection preserves the AppendFuture completion (inmem_transport.go:311-339)

evidence.reason: Returns state, term, last_log_index/term, commit_index, applied_index, snapshot indexes, latest configuration, num_peers, last_contact as a freshly built map of strings — safe by-value snapshot.
Configuration read surface backed by an atomic copy stored via Clone() (raft.go:2220), giving tests the target-native latest configuration with an instance-scoped reference.
Public observer registration; each Observation carries the concrete *Raft instance reference and target-native data, allowing tests to correlate events with the node.

observation.boundary: Public Raft accessors, observer API, and caller-owned stores inside the boundary.
observation.reason: The target exposes direct, thread-safe, target-native accessors for role, term, commit/applied index, leader identity, last contact, latest configuration, and reloadable config, plus an observer stream carrying the *Raft instance reference and a caller-owned LogStore for log ranges. No aggregation accessor is needed; the existing status interface is sufficient.
limitations: GetConfiguration/ConfigurationFuture return a Configuration whose Servers slice shares its backing array with the stored atomic copy (configuration.go:83-86 plus api.go:897-902): caller mutation of the returned slice corrupts subsequent reads of that copy, so it is not a fully deep snapshot (protocol main-loop state is unaffected).
Stats documents itself as informational/debug-only (api.go:1135-1136) and 'applied_index' may lag the FSM's actual consumption (api.go:1240-1244).
Observer channels are non-blocking by default and drop observations when full (observer.go:140-146).
entrypoints: caller-owned LogStore for log ranges (LogStore.GetLog/FirstIndex/LastIndex, log.go)
usage_examples:
st := r.Stats() // map[string]string with "state", "term", "commit_index", "applied_index"
state := r.State() // raft.Follower/Candidate/Leader
cfgF := r.GetConfiguration()
cfg := cfgF.Configuration() // raft.Configuration with Servers
observation.test_support_reason: State(), Stats(), index accessors, LeaderWithID, GetConfiguration, LastContact, LeaderCh, and the observer API are directly usable public interfaces; no target code is required for observation.
execution_paths: scalar node state: State/CurrentTerm/LastIndex/CommitIndex/AppliedIndex read atomics or locks (state.go:79-110; api.go:1102-1247)
aggregate snapshot: Stats builds a fresh map[string]string from atomics plus GetConfiguration (api.go:1160-1218)
configuration: GetConfiguration returns the cloned atomic copy of the latest configuration (raft.go:2220-2241; configuration.go:83-86)

event stream: Observer channel receives Observation{Raft: *Raft, Data: ...} for RequestVoteRequest, state changes, peer/leader changes, heartbeat failures (observer.go:120-149; raft.go:108, 614, 1605, 1738, 2157)
log range: the test reads the caller-provided LogStore (e.g., NewInmemStore) directly

evidence.reason: Global math/rand is seeded once from crypto/rand at package init; there is no per-node or injectable source, so values cannot be reproduced per instance.
All protocol-relevant timeout jitter flows through this single helper using global rand.Int63(); a config-injected source here would cover every call site.
Election timer is re-randomized on each campaign (also raft.go:353,426), so reproducibility requires controlling the source per node across repeated draws.

randomness_control.boundary: Protocol-internal randomness in the raft module (election timeout jitter, commit/snapshot staggering, in-memory address generation).
randomness_control.gap: No per-node or per-instance random source and no config/injection point; global source only, so identical initial state cannot reproduce the same per-instance election-timeout choices under concurrency.
randomness_control.reason: Protocol-relevant randomness (election timeout jitter in [HeartbeatTimeout, 2x)) comes from a single global math/rand source with no configuration or injection point. Seeding the global source from a test cannot guarantee that a specific node receives a specific timeout because concurrent goroutines across nodes draw from the same sequence in call-order-dependent fashion; per-node reproducible assignment is missing. A low-intrusion change (a Config hook or injectable rand source threaded into randomTimeout) would complete the capability while preserving the production default and the [min, 2x) domain.
limitations: NewInmemAddr and generateUUID use crypto/rand (inmem_transport.go:15-17; util.go:59-71) and are not reproducible; they do not affect protocol decisions but do affect addresses.
randomTimeout(0) returns nil (no timer) — any injected source must preserve this sentinel behavior (util.go:35-37).
Snapshot interval staggering also draws from the same source (snapshot.go:75); the control mechanism should cover all randomTimeout call sites for a coherent domain.
randomness_control.suggested_direction: Config-injected randomization hook with default unchanged; scope documented as per-node when each Raft's source is distinct.
entrypoints: randomTimeout (util.go:34) used at raft.go:163, 217, 310, 353, 426; replication.go:169, 402, 495; snapshot.go:75
package init seeding of global math/rand (util.go:18-21)
randomness_control.test_support_reason: Only a package-global seeded source exists; there is no test-visible injection point, so the existing interface is a primitive for reproducible per-instance choices.
suggested_changes: Add a Config field such as `ElectionTimeoutRandomization func(minVal time.Duration) time.Duration` (or an injectable *rand.Rand) stored in the atomic Config and used by every randomTimeout call site; keep the current global-rand behavior as the default.
Thread the same injected source through replication.go and snapshot.go staggering so the whole timing domain is controlled consistently.
execution_paths: election/heartbeat jitter: rand.Int63() draws from the process-global math/rand source seeded once in init() (util.go:18-40); each node's goroutines call randomTimeout concurrently
commit and snapshot staggering: same global source (replication.go:169,495; snapshot.go:75)
address generation: crypto/rand, not seeded (inmem_transport.go:15-17)

evidence.reason: Every protocol timer is created with time.After on the wall clock; there is no Tick surface and no injectable clock.
Heartbeat expiry is decided by comparing time.Since(lastContact) against the wall clock, so deterministic time advancement would require replacing wall-clock reads, not just timers.
The only runtime timing control is shortening configured durations (asyncNotifyCh to re-arm timers, api.go:733-739); it scales wall-clock time but cannot deterministically advance or freeze it.

time_control.boundary: Protocol loops, replication, and snapshot scheduling inside the raft module.
time_control.gap: No deterministic time control: tests can shorten timeouts via Config/ReloadConfig (wall-clock speed-up) but cannot advance or freeze protocol-observed time.
time_control.reason: Wall-clock time is dispersed throughout the protocol: timers are created via time.After inside randomTimeout and the user APIs, and expiry/contact decisions use time.Now/time.Since directly. There is no explicit Tick and no injectable Clock; shrinking Config durations only accelerates real time. Deterministic advancement would require threading an injectable clock or tick through the main loop, replication, snapshotting, and API timeouts — an invasive change, not a low-intrusion patch.
limitations: randomTimeout randomizes every interval to [minVal, 2*minVal) (util.go:33-40), so even configured durations are jittered and non-deterministic.
Config validation enforces minimums (HeartbeatTimeout >= 5ms, ElectionTimeout >= HeartbeatTimeout, CommitTimeout >= 1ms; config.go:348-374), limiting how small a test may set timers.
BatchApplyCh buffers applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and can break CommitTimeout guarantees (config.go:169-174).
time_control.suggested_direction: Injectable clock with production default of the real wall clock; coordinate with the randomness hook so jitter remains reproducible.
entrypoints: time.After / time.NewTimer usage: util.go:39 (randomTimeout), api.go:831,861,1058 (Apply/Barrier/Restore timeouts), raft.go:163-353 (heartbeat/election), replication.go:169,402,495, snapshot.go:75
time.Now / time.Since: api.go:1128 (LastContact), api.go:1215 (Stats), raft.go:221 (contact check), future.go:135 (dispatch), replication.go:416 (LastContact observation)
Config.HeartbeatTimeout / ElectionTimeout / CommitTimeout / LeaderLeaseTimeout / SnapshotInterval (config.go:149-205) with ReloadConfig (api.go:717-741)
time_control.test_support_reason: Only wall-clock duration configuration exists; no Tick or Clock abstraction is exposed, so the existing interface is not a complete deterministic time-control interface.
suggested_changes: Introduce an injectable clock (interface with Now() and After()) threaded into Raft and its Config, replacing direct time.After/time.Now/time.Since in raft.go, replication.go, snapshot.go, future.go, and api.go timeout paths.
Alternatively expose an explicit Tick/step mechanism on the main loop, converting timer channels into tick counters — a larger structural change affecting runFollower/runCandidate/runLeader.
execution_paths: election/heartbeat timers: randomTimeout builds time.After channels (raft.go:163,217,310,353,426)
commit timer: randomTimeout(CommitTimeout) in replication loops (replication.go:169,495)
snapshot check timer: randomTimeout(SnapshotInterval) (snapshot.go:75)
user-API timeouts: time.After in Apply/Barrier/Restore/requestConfigChange (api.go:831,861,1058; raft.go:117-119)
wall-clock observations: time.Now/time.Since for lastContact staleness (raft.go:221, api.go:1128-1132, 1215)
